name: Tàihé A Bāo 泰和A包
description: Tàihé A Bāo (泰和A包) is a Chinese climbing game from Taihe county, Jiangxi province. Four players: one declarer vs the other three each hand. 40-card deck (remove 2s, 3s, 8s); rank A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 7, 6, 5, 4. Cards drawn from deck counterclockwise (not dealt). Bidding: declare or pass; if all pass, second round—call for a card (exchange); last caller is declarer. Play: declarer leads combinations; others beat or pass. Combinations: singles, pairs, sequences, double sequences, three-of-a-kind, four-of-a-kind (bombs beat any non-bomb). First out wins; if declarer wins they collect stakes from each opponent. Often played for money.

history.origins: Chinese climbing game from Taihe (泰和) county, Jiangxi (江西) province. A correspondent learned it there around 2013. Name refers to the Ace (A) as highest card. Part of the broader Chinese climbing/shedding family.
timeline: Learned in Taihe county, Jiangxi, c.2013
Documented in English-language climbing games literature

setup.dealing: The deck is shuffled and placed face-down in the center. Each player receives 10 cards by taking one card at a time in turn in counterclockwise order.

rules.objective: As declarer, be the first to empty your hand to win and collect stakes from each opponent; as an opponent, empty your hand first to make the declarer lose and pay each of you.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal: Each player takes 10 cards one at a time in counterclockwise order from the face-down deck. 2. Bidding round 1: In turn, each player may declare (become declarer; play starts immediately) or pass. 3. If all pass, bidding round 2: Each may call for a card (name rank and suit; holder gives it face-up, you give one face-down in exchange) or pass; last player to call is declarer. If all pass again, redeal. 4. Play: Declarer leads any legal combination. Each in turn may beat it (same type, higher rank) or pass. Three consecutive passes clear the table; the last player to have played leads any legal combination. 5. First player out of cards wins the hand: if declarer, they win; if an opponent, declarer loses. Stakes are paid per opponent based on how many called in bidding.
keyRules: Combinations: single, pair, sequence (3+ consecutive ranks; Aces not in sequences; 7 and 9 not consecutive), double sequence, three-of-a-kind, four-of-a-kind. Three- and four-of-a-kind (bombs) beat any non-bomb.
Rank order high to low: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 7, 6, 5, 4. Suits do not affect rank.

Hand value in stakes: if declarer called for a card, value = number of players who called; if declarer declared in round 1, value = number of players plus one. Declarer wins or loses that many stakes to each opponent.

strategy.basic: Lead low combinations to force opponents to use high cards; save bombs (three- or four-of-a-kind) to regain the lead when needed.
strategy.intermediate: Count cards and track which combinations have been played; time your passes to let others burn high cards.
strategy.advanced: As declarer, open with combinations that split opponents; as opponents, coordinate to exhaust declarer's bombs before going out.
tips: In the second bidding round, call for a card that completes a strong combination or blocks the declarer.

variations.name: Five players
variations.description: Five players; each receives eight cards. A hand declared in the first round of bidding is worth six stakes against each opponent.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes player count and stake value; engine constants could be added when implementing.

variations.name: Three players
variations.description: Remove the Ace of Spades; 39 cards. Each player receives 13 cards. A set of three Aces counts as four Aces (unbeatable). First-round declare worth four stakes per opponent.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes deck size and special combo rule; overrides can be added at implementation time.

variations.name: Without Aces
variations.description: Kings are highest. Kings may be exchanged in bidding and used in sequences. Five players: also remove King of Spades, seven cards each. Three players: 12 cards each, deck otherwise unchanged.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes rank set and deck composition; overrides for deck and rank when building.
